comment: THE sentence rule, specified once. splitSentences() in graph/sentences.ts and split_sentences() in tools/sentences.py must agree on every case here. Sentences TILE their paragraph — contiguous, gapless, trailing whitespace belonging to the sentence it follows — so joining them returns the paragraph byte for byte. That identity is why accepting one sentence cannot reflow its neighbours. THE BIAS: when unsure, do not split. An unsplit pair costs a coarser judgment; a wrong split costs half a sentence landing in the author's book. Run: npm test (graph/) and python3 tools/test_sentence_vectors.py. Sections: splits (expected sentence texts, both languages) and offsets (start/end pairs, both languages).

splits.why: the ordinary case — two plain sentences
splits.paragraph: He shipped the oars. The swell ran heavy out of the north.
sentences: The swell ran heavy out of the north.

splits.why: no terminal punctuation at all — the paragraph is one sentence
splits.paragraph: Green rot and woodsmoke over the water
sentences: Green rot and woodsmoke over the water

splits.why: fragments, the house style — each still a sentence
splits.paragraph: Green rot. Woodsmoke. Rain drying on hot stone.

splits.why: an abbreviation mid-sentence does not end it
splits.paragraph: Mr. Reyes went down to the water. He did not look back.
sentences: Mr. Reyes went down to the water.

splits.paragraph: J. R. R. Tolkien wrote it. Then he revised it.
sentences: J. R. R. Tolkien wrote it.

splits.why: a year or decimal is not a boundary, but the sentence's own period is
splits.paragraph: The seed came ashore in 1848. It measured 3.14 centimetres.

splits.why: an ellipsis trails off; it never terminates (deliberate under-split)
splits.paragraph: He waited... then the light came back. The sea turned to tin.
sentences: He waited... then the light came back.

splits.why: a unicode ellipsis behaves the same as three dots
splits.paragraph: He waited… then he rowed. The coast held.

splits.why: an em-dash is never a terminator
splits.paragraph: The boat rode low — heavy with water — and he bailed. Then he slept.
sentences: The boat rode low — heavy with water — and he bailed.

splits.why: the quotation case: the mark belongs to the quote, the speech tag continues it
splits.paragraph: "Get out!" he said. The door stood open.

splits.why: a quotation that ends the sentence outright, capital following
curly quotes close a sentence exactly as straight ones do

splits.paragraph: Where was he? Nobody knew! The tide came in.

splits.why: no space after the period — not a boundary
splits.paragraph: The file was named scene.md and nothing else.
sentences: The file was named scene.md and nothing else.

splits.why: a closing paren after the terminal mark travels with its sentence
splits.paragraph: He left at dawn (before the others woke.) The camp stayed quiet.
sentences: He left at dawn (before the others woke.)

splits.why: multiple spaces between sentences belong to the first — rejoin must be lossless
splits.paragraph: He shipped the oars.  Salt burned in the cracks.

splits.why: trailing whitespace at the end of a paragraph is kept
an empty paragraph has no sentences

splits.paragraph: He brought rope, tin, etc. and left the rest behind.
sentences: He brought rope, tin, etc. and left the rest behind.

offsets.why: offsets tile the paragraph with no gaps
offsets.paragraph: He shipped the oars. The swell ran heavy.
"Get out!" he said. The door stood open.
